anomalies.obs: On the SkylabModule sheet, NET0044 is the load-switch gate node: it joins U11.31 (P4_LED/GPIO) to Q1.1 (NTR2101P gate) and to the R3 10k pull-up to +3V3, while Q1.3 (drain) is NET0036 (the Display_Power_Switch). On the EPD_Driver sheet, NET0044 instead appears on the boost-converter power/switching node (L2 10uH input, C13/C15, and the panel VDD/VDDIO pins J6.15/16), and NET0036 (the actual Display_Power_Switch) does not appear anywhere in the EPD_Driver sheet.
anomalies.exp: Per the spec, Q2's drain (Display_Power_Switch) must feed J1.15/16 and the boost L1/C1/C2, and Q2's gate must be the separate GPIO net (U5.31) pulled up by R2. The gate net and the display-power/boost node must be two distinct nets; the EPD rail must be the drain net (NET0036), not the gate net (NET0044).

evidence.quote: SkylabModule sheet: R3 10k between +3V3 and Q1.1; Q1.1 wired to U11.31 with label NET0044; Q1.3 label NET0036
EPD_Driver sheet: NET0044 wired to L2 (10uH) input / C13 / C15 and the panel VDD node; no NET0036 present on the sheet
Q2.3 (drain) ties to the Display_Power_Switch net, which feeds J1.15/J1.16 ... plus the EPD boost converter's L1, C1, C2 ... R2 (10 kΩ, pulling Q2's gate high/off by default), and U5.31 ... gate

anomalies.impact: The high-side display power MOSFET (Q1) no longer gates the EPD rail: the panel VDD/boost input is tied to the 3.3V GPIO gate net, so the leakage-prevention switch is ineffective (panel is always powered / never switched off), and the GPIO driving the gate is shorted to the boost converter's switching/power node. This can prevent correct display power sequencing and risks overheating/damage of the power switch (cf. commit b3a898a 'Display Power MOSFET heats up').

parsed.summary: Reference designators are renumbered relative to the spec (a benign build difference), but the EPD power-switching net is mis-routed: the load-switch gate net (NET0044) is bridged onto the EPD boost/panel-VDD node, while the load-switch drain (NET0036 / Display_Power_Switch) never reaches the EPD sheet, contradicting the spec's intended gate-vs-drain separation.
